data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, rabbi means 'my teacher'. This title has been used in Jewish and Christian traditions to refer to spiritual leaders and teachers. The name Rabbi carries the meaning “My teacher” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rabbi usually hope their child will grow to embody my teacher and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Rabbi belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My teacher.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rabbi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: רַבִי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word רב (rav) meaning 'great' or 'master'. In the context of religious teachers, it came to mean 'my great one' or 'my master'. It's also a title of respect for elders or leaders.

in_greek.name: ραββί
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Aramaic word רבי (rabbi) which was adopted in Greek. It's equivalent to the Greek word διδάσκαλος (didaskalos) meaning 'teacher'.

in_latin.name: Rabbi
in_latin.long_meaning: Adopted directly from the Greek ραββί (rabbi) and the Hebrew רב (rav). It's equivalent to the Latin word magister or doctor, meaning 'teacher' or 'master'.

in_english.name: Rabbi
in_english.long_meaning: Adopted directly from the Hebrew רבי (rabbi) and the Aramaic רַבָּא (rabbā). It's a title of respect for religious teachers and leaders.

data.cultural_impact: The title 'Rabbi' has its roots in Jewish tradition, where it was used to refer to scholars, teachers, and spiritual leaders. However, the title has also been adopted and used in certain Christian communities, particularly within the Messianic Jewish and Hebrew Roots movements. These communities seek to connect their Christian faith with Jewish heritage and traditions, and the use of the title 'Rabbi' is one way to bridge that gap. By using the term, they are acknowledging the importance of spiritual teachers and leaders within their faith community.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the title 'Rabbi' signifies a teacher, guide, and mentor. This title carries with it a deep sense of respect and acknowledgement of the knowledge and wisdom that the one bearing the title possesses. 'Rabbi' implies a level of commitment and dedication to the spiritual and intellectual growth of those being taught, as well as a deep connection to the religious traditions and teachings of one's faith community. In both the Jewish and Christian traditions, the role of the rabbi is not only to impart knowledge but also to provide spiritual guidance and support to those seeking to deepen their faith and live according to the teachings of their faith.
